rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase; utility add-on eliminated
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be raised once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD. Effective February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer add an extra percentage increase for utilities.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the LAHD allowable rent increase percentage; no utility add-on from 2026-02-02
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LAMC Chapter XV)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.coverage_text: Generally, the RSO applies to rental properties that were first built on or before October 1, 1978, as well as replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28; includes apartments, condominiums and townhomes (rent not regulated for tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995), duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, hotel/motel rooms occupied more than 30 consecutive days, ADUs, JADUs, mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks.
rules.exemptions: Rent may reset to market rate after voluntary vacancy, certain at-fault evictions, City Attorney order evictions, or a Tenant Buyout Agreement. Condominium and townhome rent not regulated for tenancies commenced after December 31, 1995. Luxury exemption available on application.
rules.extraction_note: The page is an LAHD summary and does not state the percentage itself (it refers to a separate PDF) and gives no LAMC section for the annual increase. The 2026-02-02 effective date applies to the elimination of the utility add-on, not to the underlying 12-month rule. The page also notes a rent freeze from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024. The page lists several LAHD-approved increase programs (capital improvement, primary renovation, seismic retrofit, rehabilitation, just and reasonable). It also lists permitted surcharges: registration, Systematic Code Enforcement Fee, and smoke detector.

rules.title: RSO additional occupant rent increase; dependent increase eliminated
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, landlords may not impose a 10% increase for an additional dependent added to an RSO tenancy. A 10% increase is still allowed for an additional non-dependent tenant if imposed within 60 days of the landlord learning of that tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% per additional non-dependent tenant; 0% for dependents from 2026-02-02
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LAMC Chapter XV)
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the RSO (generally built on or before October 1, 1978).
rules.extraction_note: No LAMC section is given on the page. The quoted span preserves the source's misspelling 'additonal'.

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction, notice, and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenancies may be terminated only for listed at-fault causes (e.g., nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance, illegal use, refusal of access) or no-fault causes (owner/family move-in, resident manager, demolition/removal from market, government order, conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict, 30- or 60-day written notice (some require 120 days or up to a 1-year extension), and payment of relocation assistance. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: Enumerated just causes; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions; 30/60-day notice (some 120 days or 1-year extension)
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance (generally built on or before October 1, 1978); non-RSO properties are covered by the separate Just Cause Ordinance.
rules.extraction_note: Relocation assistance amounts are not stated on the page. The cited LAMC sections relate to the notice-filing requirement. Beginning August 20, 2025, a Notice of Right to Counsel must be attached to eviction notices. The page has no effective date for the eviction rules themselves.
